title: Introduce perturbation-based smoke suite and progressive escalation for prompt-set regressions
author: Asha Patel
ci_checks: unit-tests: passed (run-441) flaky-tests: rerun and passed
integration-smoke: passed on ubuntu-20/ubuntu-22 matrix after fix
body: Motivation: CI currently gates prompt-set regressions using aggregate eval metrics which sometimes miss brittle regressions caused by small input perturbations or prompt paraphrases. This PR adds a perturbation-based smoke suite that generates lightweight synthetic variants of critical prompt sets (token-level shuffles, polite/impolite paraphrases, punctuation/noise insertion, and casing variants) and a progressive escalation policy that turns single-test failures into graduated CI outcomes: warn -> soft-fail -> hard-fail, depending on historical stability and threshold breaches. Design: 1) new module perturbation_suite that plugs into existing eval harness runner and exposes a declarative YAML to define perturbation families and generation ratios; 2) lightweight scoring adapter that computes delta-against-baseline using existing metrics (exact match, semantic-similarity embedding score, and response-structure checks) and emits a compact JSON report suitable for CI summaries; 3) escalation controller that consults cohort stability metadata (from the eval registry) and decides when to surface failures as warnings vs blocker failures; 4) CI integration hook that folds the report into GitHub checks UI and optionally annotates affected prompt IDs. Backwards compatibility: the perturbation suite is opt-in and disabled by default for existing repos; project-level config can enable it per-prompt-set and tune escalation thresholds. Rollout plan: enable on Canary projects for 2 weeks, monitor false-positive rate, adjust perturbation families. Docs & links: internal design doc https://linear.app/ENG/1123/perturbation-smoke-suite and example config in docs/perturbations.md. Checklist: - [x] unit tests for generator edge-cases - [x] integration test for CI annotation - [x] documentation and example config - [x] feature flagged in config schema - [x] Linear tasks linked. Impact: expected to catch ~65% of small-paraphrase regressions observed historically during retros, avoid noisy full-eval runs for low-severity regressions, and provide actionable prompt-level traces for owners.

review_comments: Devon Clarke: Nice separation of generator and scorer. Two asks: make generator deterministic by default in CI runs, and add a config knob to limit total generated variants per PR to avoid expensive runs.
Asha Patel (author): Made seed deterministic when CI=true and added max_variants config with default=20. Updated tests to assert determinism.
Riley Chen: Scoring thresholds look strict for semantic similarity; asked for a tuning guide and a soft-fail threshold to prevent noisy hard-fails.
Asha Patel: Added escalation controller logic and an internal tuning guide in docs; soft-fail introduced for first breach, hard-fail after repeat breaches in the last 7 days.
Priya Narang: Please ensure the GitHub annotation payload does not include PII or customer data. Also requested unit for annotation sanitization.
Asha Patel: Added sanitization step and unit test; verified that only prompt IDs and diff-level hashes are published.
CI flakiness note: initial integration matrix failed on ubuntu-20 due to a dependency mismatch, rerun passed after pinned dependency; logs attached in CI run-439.
release_notes: Add an opt-in perturbation-based smoke suite for prompt-sets that generates synthetic variants and applies a progressive escalation policy (warn -> soft-fail -> hard-fail). Feature is disabled by default; enable per-project via configs/default_eval_config.yaml. Includes CI annotations and a tuning guide.
testing_instructions: Run unit tests: pytest tests/perturbation -q to validate generator and scorer behavior
CI sanity: verify GitHub check shows annotation summary and 'soft-fail' warning instead of hard fail on first breach
rationale: Small paraphrases and token-level perturbations have historically caused production regressions that aggregate metrics miss; a targeted, low-cost synthetic suite that escalates failures gradually gives prompt owners immediate, actionable traces while reducing noisy full-eval runs.
